params.pairing: weeks where both series have a value

quantities.name: rate30_latest
quantities.meaning: 30-year rate in the last paired week.

quantities.name: rate15_latest
quantities.meaning: 15-year rate in the last paired week.

quantities.name: pay15_latest
quantities.meaning: Latest paired week 2026-09-24: 30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%. Payment on a 15-year loan (n=180) at the 15-year rate, rounded to cents.

quantities.name: pay30on15_latest
quantities.meaning: Latest paired week 2026-09-24: 30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%. Payment that retires the 30-year loan in 15 years: level payment with n=180 at the 30-year rate, rounded to cents.

quantities.name: pay30_latest
quantities.meaning: Latest paired week 2026-09-24: 30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%. Required payment on the 30-year loan (n=360) at the 30-year rate, rounded to cents.

quantities.name: extra_month_latest
quantities.meaning: Latest paired week 2026-09-24: 30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%. pay30on15 minus pay15 (unrounded), rounded to cents.

quantities.name: extra_total_latest
quantities.meaning: Latest paired week 2026-09-24: 30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%. (pay30on15 - pay15) * 180 using unrounded payments, rounded to whole dollars: extra paid over 15 years for paying the 30-year loan on a 15-year schedule.

quantities.name: months_payoff_at_pay15
quantities.meaning: Latest paired week 2026-09-24: 30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%. Months to pay off the 30-year loan at the 30-year rate if the borrower pays exactly the 15-year payment (unrounded): n = -ln(1 - P*x/pay15)/ln(1+x), rounded to 0.1.

quantities.name: spread_mean
quantities.meaning: Spread = 30-year rate - 15-year rate per paired week; mean of spreads, rounded to 0.01.

quantities.name: spread_min
quantities.meaning: Smallest weekly spread (30-year minus 15-year), rounded to 0.01.

quantities.name: spread_max
quantities.meaning: Largest weekly spread (30-year minus 15-year), rounded to 0.01.

quantities.name: share_spread_ge_050
quantities.meaning: Share of paired weeks with spread >= 0.50 point, rounded to 0.001.

quantities.name: extra_total_median
quantities.meaning: For every paired week: (payment at the 30-year rate with n=180 - payment at the 15-year rate with n=180) * 180. Median over weeks, rounded to whole dollars.

quantities.name: extra_total_min
quantities.meaning: Same weekly quantity as extra_total_median; minimum over weeks, rounded to whole dollars.

quantities.name: extra_total_max
quantities.meaning: Same weekly quantity as extra_total_median; maximum over weeks, rounded to whole dollars.

newKindNeeds.inputs: Two weekly rate series in percent (FRED CSV: observation_date, value; blank or '.' = missing): long-term rate r30 (MORTGAGE30US) and short-term rate r15 (MORTGAGE15US). Principal P, short term n_s=180 months, long term n_l=360 months.
newKindNeeds.computation: Pair weeks where both rates exist. For each week w: level payment pay(r,n)=P*x/(1-(1+x)^-n), x=r/1200. Short loan pay(r15,180); long loan paid on the short schedule pay(r30,180); long loan required pay(r30,360). extra_total(w)=(pay(r30,180)-pay(r15,180))*180. Months to pay off the long loan at the short-loan payment: n=-ln(1-P*x/pay15)/ln(1+x). Spread(w)=r30-r15.
newKindNeeds.outputs: Per-week extra_total, spread; summary: count of paired weeks, first/last week, latest-week payments and extra cost, months_at_pay15, spread mean/min/max/share>=0.5, extra_total median/min/max with weeks; optional: monthly simulation with yearly lump vs monthly extra (episode ep007).
newKindNeeds.invariants: pay(r30,180) >= pay(r15,180) whenever r30 >= r15; extra_total is increasing in the spread at a given level; pay(r30,360) < pay(r15,180) for all weeks in the data; months_at_pay15 > 180 iff r30 > r15; no rounding before outputs; paired weeks only (1991-08-30 onward).
newKindNeeds.dataNow: sources.json lastObservation 2026-09-24 (dossier pin); episode ep007 refreshes to 2026-10-08 (episodes/ep007/data/sources.json).
